issue.title: Re-budget the Python 3.13 test-cost CI lane
issue.description: Scheduled Full CI repeatedly times out the Python 3.13 test-cost lane at the old 90-minute ceiling. This unblock raises the workflow timeout to 150 minutes because the lane appears to need roughly two hours, but the durable fix is to re-budget, shard, or otherwise reduce the lane instead of relying on ever-growing headroom.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: This is not intermittent: scheduled Full CI consistently times out the Python 3.13 test-cost leg at the 90-minute ceiling on master SHA 7420b8298 and later, with the suite about 73-74 percent complete at timeout and an extrapolated runtime near two hours. The 3.12 and 3.14 legs finish; only the heavier 3.13 cost lane has outgrown the old budget.

evidence.note: Independent evidence proposed by sase-xe.16.11.7.16.5.3: check-full run 20260915T170253Z completed 41,756 tests (21 skipped) but the test-cost hard-budget gate measured total_file_cpu_seconds=6703s versus 3250s tolerated, with multiple Ace/Textual/parser/YAML buckets over budget. This corroborates that the lane needs durable re-budgeting/sharding rather than more timeout headroom.
